artists.biography:
C.O.C. started out as a punk band. The members were all teenagers during its original formation in 1981. On their later releases, they became a crossover/thrash metal band, and then turned into their modern sound, blending heavy metal with southern rock and Blues.

C.O.C. has been on hiatus many times, mostly due to the members concentrating on their own projects. Their last hiatus took place from 2006 to 2010. They have not released an official statement regarding Pepper's status in the band. Their official Facebook page lists the line-up as the above (Woody, Mike, Reed and Pepper). As the Mike/Woody/Reed lineup released a new single "Your Tomorrow" and managed to record a new album, it seems Pepper is still in the band but is not currently participating in it. C.O.C themselves have even stated that Pepper has never left the band.

Corrosion Of Conformity.biography:
C.O.C. started out as a punk band. The members were all teenagers during its original formation in 1981. On their later releases, they became a crossover/thrash metal band, and then turned into their modern sound, blending heavy metal with southern rock and Blues.

C.O.C. has been on hiatus many times, mostly due to the members concentrating on their own projects. Their last hiatus took place from 2006 to 2010. They have not released an official statement regarding Pepper's status in the band. Their official Facebook page lists the line-up as the above (Woody, Mike, Reed and Pepper). As the Mike/Woody/Reed lineup released a new single "Your Tomorrow" and managed to record a new album, it seems Pepper is still in the band but is not currently participating in it. C.O.C themselves have even stated that Pepper has never left the band.

perplexity.description:
Wiseblood, released in October 1996, is the fifth studio album by American rock band Corrosion of Conformity. Musically, it continues the heavy, groove-oriented metal and blues-infused rock style the band had developed on their previous album Deliverance (1994), blending aggressive riffs with organic grooves and a raw, abrasive sound. The album features a mix of heavy metal and blues influences, maintaining the band's integrity despite major label pressures to soften their sound or use outside songwriting help.

In Corrosion of Conformity's discography, Wiseblood represents a consolidation of their shift toward a more accessible yet still heavy and uncompromising style, with Pepper Keenan firmly established as lead vocalist. It was their highest-charting album in the U.S. at the time, peaking at number 104 on the Billboard 200, and included the single "Drowning in a Daydream," which received significant rock radio airplay and earned a Grammy nomination for Best Metal Performance in 1998. Despite this, the album did not match the commercial success of Deliverance, selling over 140,000 copies by 2002. Notably, Metallica's James Hetfield contributed backing vocals on the album, underscoring its connection to the broader metal community.
